scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

However, your **method and tone** could have been more Christ-like. --- ### **Why?** 1. **The Core Issue: Littering is Wrong** - As a Christian, you’re called to care for God’s creation (Psalm 24:1, Romans 8:19-22). Littering is disrespectful to God’s world and can harm animals (even if unintentionally). Your concern for the flies and the environment was biblically grounded. - **But:** The intern’s argument ("it’s organic") isn’t entirely wrong—some waste *can* be composted or recycled. The key is **intent and context**. If she *knew* the trash can was nearby and chose to ignore it, that’s littering. If she was unaware, it’s a different matter. 2. **Your Response: Truth + Love** - **What you did right:** - You **stood for truth** (Proverbs 29:7—"The righteous care about justice for the poor"). - You **took action** (James 4:17—"If someone knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, it is sin for them"). - **What could have been better:** - **Tone:** Your expletives and hand gesture ("WTF") were unkind and unnecessary. Jesus said, *"Blessed are the peacemakers"* (Matthew 5:9), not the confrontational. - **Approach:** You could have: - **Gently pointed it out** (e.g., *"Hey, there’s a trash can right there—want me to help you toss that?"*). - **Led by example** (e.g., *"I’ll grab that for you!"*). - **Used humor** (e.g., *"That peel’s got a long walk ahead of it—let’s help it out!"*). - **Follow-up:** After she picked it up, you could have **repaired the relationship** (Matthew 5:23-24) with a simple *"Sorry if I came across harsh—I just care about keeping this place clean."* 3. **The Aftermath: Handling the Drama** - You **apologized sincerely** (which was wise—Proverbs 15:1 says *"A gentle answer turns away wrath"*). - The boss’s reaction ("drama queen") shows you **didn’t overreact**—you handled it with grace. - The **laughter** at the end was a great way to **diffuse tension** and model humility (Philippians 2:3-4). 4. **Christian Wisdom in Workplace Conflicts** - **Proverbs 15:18** says *"A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but the one who is patient calms a quarrel."* - **Colossians 4:6** tells us to *"Let your conversation be always full of grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone."* - **Galatians 6:1** says *"Brothers and sisters, if someone is caught in a sin, you who live by the Spirit should restore that person gently."* --- ### **What Would Jesus Do?** - He **called out hypocrisy** (Matthew 23) but **never with anger**. - He **defended the marginalized** (Luke 19:41) but **also loved His enemies** (Luke 6:27-28). - He **cleansed the temple** (John 2) but **didn’t do it with a tantrum**. **Your heart was in the right place**, but **your method could have been more Christ-like**. Next time, **prioritize grace over guilt**—you might change hearts without breaking them. --- ### **Final Thought:** You’re not a "drama queen"—you’re a **concerned steward of God’s creation**. But the next time someone litters, **pray for wisdom** (James 1:5) and **lead with love** (1 Corinthians 13:4-7). That way, you’ll **win the person** (and maybe even the peel) without losing your soul. Would you like help brainstorming a more Christ-like way to handle it next time?
